scope: Source evidence for feeding, preventive care, emergencies, breed risks, ACT rules, and Cats.com reading links. This is not clinical review or approval of the whole app.
method: Read project content JSON, src/health.ts, and src/feeding.ts. Read fetched public pages and relevant sections of official PDFs. Search results were used for discovery only unless an access failure is stated. PDF quotations have whitespace and mathematical glyphs normalized.

sources.title: Energy Requirement Calculations — Box 1, 2021 AAHA Nutrition and Weight Management Guidelines
sources.readStatus: Official one-page PDF downloaded and read with pdftotext
sources.locator: Box 1: formula, feline column, and footnote
excerpts: RER = BWkg^0.75 × 70
MER = RER × life stage factor
Neutered adults 1.2–1.4
Intact adult 1.4–1.6
Inactive/obese prone 1.0
Weight loss 0.8
Growth 2.5
Adjustment of caloric intake should be done by monitoring BW and BCS.
sources.limits: Starting estimates, not prescriptions. The feline growth column does not split at four months; that split belongs to dogs. The table does not assign normal activity to the low end or high activity to the high end of adult ranges.
recommendedCorrections: Keep the current feline factors and kilogram units. Identify activity-to-range selection as an app assumption.
Exclude pregnancy, lactation, illness, and pre-weaning kittens from a general solid-food calculator. Box 1 has separate gestation and lactation factors.

sources.title: Feeding Plans for Healthy, Appropriate Weight Cats and Dogs
sources.readStatus: Page body read
excerpts: Calculate current caloric intake from all food items.
the main source of complete and balanced nutrition represents ≥90% of total intake whereas treats and other food items make up ≤10%
Owner assessment of these parameters should be verified by a member of the veterinary team.
sources.limits: The 10% limit is calories, not grams or food volume. It is a ceiling, not a required treat allowance. Food used for medication also counts.
recommendedCorrections: State that treats and extras come from the daily calorie allowance, not on top of it.
If a treat allowance is calculated, subtract it before wet/dry portion conversion. Do not subtract 10% automatically if no treats are fed.

sources.title: Weight Reduction in the Obese Pet
sources.readStatus: Page body and embedded Box 1 read
excerpts: Base these calculations on ideal weight and adjust as needed for the individual patient, based on current intake and lifestyle needs.
sources.limits: The 2021 page refers readers to the 2014 weight-management guideline for detailed monitoring. Its HTML table omits the neutered-adult row; the official Box 1 PDF includes it.
recommendedCorrections: Keep the vet-set target weight requirement. Do not use current overweight body weight in the 0.8 × RER weight-loss estimate.
Replace any claim of an exact duration to target with a clearly labelled illustration, or omit it.

sources.title: Section 8: Dietary Management — 2026 AAHA Diabetes Management Guidelines for Cats
sources.readStatus: Dietary Therapy Goals and Management section read
excerpts: a healthy rate of loss for an obese cat is 0.5–2% of body weight per week
sources.limits: This guideline concerns diabetic cats. The cited range is a monitored clinical goal for obese cats, not a guaranteed response to any calculator result.
recommendedCorrections: State the 0.5–2% range with vet supervision. The app's fixed 1% value is an illustrative assumption within that range, not a predicted result.
Use an exact rate source rather than saying the range appears in AAHA 2021 Box 1.

sources.title: Management of obesity in cats
sources.publisher: Veterinary Medicine: Research and Reports; Hoelmkjaer and Bjornvad
sources.readStatus: Weight-loss plan, target weight, energy restriction, and follow-up sections read
excerpts: Generally, weight loss in cats should aim at a rate of 0.5%–2% of initial BW per week
each unit increase in BCS above ideal approximates an increase in BW of 10%–15% compared with ideal
BCS scoring is however imprecise in extremely obese cats
sources.limits: Peer-reviewed review, not a new trial. It cites AAHA 2014 for the loss range. It supports approximate BCS-to-weight relationships, not an exact target-weight conversion. Calorie restriction can cause nutrient deficiency and hepatic lipidosis.
recommendedCorrections: Keep target weight as a vet-set input. Avoid claiming that no BCS-to-weight estimate exists; instead say a score alone does not give a reliable individual target.
Tell owners to use a diet suitable for supervised weight loss, rather than simply cutting any maintenance diet.
Do not allow a weight-loss result to imply safe restriction for an underweight cat or growing kitten.

sources.title: 2024 guidelines for the vaccination of dogs and cats — compiled by the Vaccination Guidelines Group of WSAVA
sources.readStatus: Official PDF downloaded; feline table and feline vaccination sections read with pdftotext
sources.locator: Vaccination of cats; feline core and non-core vaccine table; FIV discussion
excerpts: Immunity against FCV and FHV is only partial
For ‘higher-risk’ cats more frequent revaccination to protect against FCV and FHV (up to annually) may be warranted.
These recommendations about revaccination frequency apply to MLV vaccines.
Only uninfected cats should be vaccinated.

supports.fivRevaccination: One year after the initial series, then annually for continuing exposure risk

sources.limits: FPV protection is long-lived after effective MLV immunisation. FHV/FCV protection is incomplete and is not equivalent to protection from infection or carrier status. Low-risk means more than indoor housing: boarding and contact with potentially infected cats matter. Product type, label, country, history, and risk change the plan. FeLV is core for young cats and exposed adults where FeLV disease is endemic. FIV is non-core; evidence of efficacy varies. Avoiding exposure is best.
recommendedCorrections: Replace the blanket adult F3 three-year sentence. Distinguish FPV from risk-dependent FHV/FCV intervals.
Prefer the 26-week revaccination recommendation over presenting 6–12 months as equivalent WSAVA timing.
Add boarding, other-cat exposure, vaccine history, and product type to the vet discussion. An indoor/outdoor/enclosure selector alone cannot choose vaccine frequency.
For FIV, include testing before vaccination, three initial doses, continuing exposure assessment, incomplete protection, and test interpretation. Do not list FIV as protection for every outdoor cat.
Discuss FeLV separately when exposure and local epidemiology warrant it. Do not import US availability or rabies rules into an Australian schedule.

sources.title: 2021 AAHA/AAFP Feline Life Stage Guidelines
sources.publisher: AAHA and American Association of Feline Practitioners
sources.readStatus: Official PDF downloaded; life stages and examination-frequency text read
excerpts: senior, aged over 10 years
Senior cats should be seen at least every 6 months
The Task Force recommends a minimum of annual examinations for all cats
sources.limits: The current catvets.com overview says '10 years and older', whereas the published guideline says 'over 10 years'. Do not hide this boundary difference. The 11-year cutoff in feeding.ts is a simplified whole-year label and does not cover all cats aged over 10 years. Check-up frequency is a minimum; diagnostic tests need an individual plan.
recommendedCorrections: Use the published guideline's age boundary, or explain the simplified label. For continuous ageMonths, over 120 months is not the same as 132 months or older.
Add the mature-adult stage if the UI claims to show all AAHA/AAFP life stages.
Keep annual examinations and at least six-monthly senior reviews. Phrase blood tests and blood pressure as vet-planned screening, not a universal fixed prescription.
sources.overviewReadStatus: Read current page body, including the inconsistent senior label

sources.title: AAFP and ISFM Feline Environmental Needs Guidelines
sources.publisher: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery; AAFP and ISFM
sources.readStatus: Five pillars, resource separation, predatory play, DIY feeders, and toy safety sections read
excerpts: Food and water resources should be separated from each other.
Do not force interaction with a cat.
Let the cat catch the toy on the end of the rod or wand to simulate a capture
All toys with string or other parts that can potentially be ingested by the cat should be put away after play.

pillars: Respect for the sense of smell

sources.limits: The guideline does not establish a universal 10–15-minute twice-daily play dose. Session length and intensity need to fit age, mobility, and the cat's response. A post-play treat still counts within the daily calorie budget.
recommendedCorrections: Keep hiding places, scratching, food puzzles, a final toy catch, and string-toy storage advice.
Mark suggested play duration as a starting routine, not a veterinary minimum. Stop if the cat tires or has breathing difficulty.
Separate food, water, and litter in the starter room. Give multiple cats separate resources.
Treat exact tooth-brushing training dates and durations as examples. They were not validated in this source.

sources.title: Feline Lower Urinary Tract Disease
sources.readStatus: Clinical Signs and Urethral Obstruction sections read
excerpts: A urethral obstruction is an absolute emergency, requiring immediate veterinary treatment.
will pass little or no urine and will become increasingly distressed
sources.limits: Straining can have other causes, but owners cannot safely rule out obstruction at home. Male and neutered male cats have higher obstruction risk.
recommendedCorrections: Keep immediate emergency action. Replace the unverified GSVS source string with this exact Cornell URL.

sources.title: Dyspnea (Difficulty Breathing)
sources.readStatus: Page body read
excerpts: Any time there’s a question about an animal’s ability to breathe comfortably, get it to a veterinarian right away.
sources.limits: The guessed /feline-health-topics/dyspnea URL returned 404; /node/4087 returned the full page. This source does not support waiting a few minutes to see whether abnormal breathing settles.
recommendedCorrections: Remove 'panting that doesn't settle within a few minutes' and reassurance about panting after play or travel from the emergency card.
Use immediate veterinary contact for open-mouth or laboured breathing. Keep handling calm and minimal; do not attempt home treatment.

sources.title: Anorexia
sources.readStatus: Page body read
excerpts: anorexia can have a severe impact on a mature cat’s health if it persists for as little as 24 hours
For a kitten younger than six weeks of age, food avoidance for just 12 hours can pose a lethal threat.
sources.limits: Cornell advises immediate consultation on noticing anorexia. Twenty-four hours is a risk threshold, not advice to wait. This page does not establish that hepatic lipidosis always starts after one or two days.
recommendedCorrections: Change the title from 'more than 24 hours' to advice to contact the vet promptly when the cat stops eating. Make 24 hours a clear adult warning and seek advice sooner for kittens or ill cats.
Replace the exact one-to-two-day fatty-liver claim with 'Not eating can cause serious illness, including hepatic lipidosis.'

sources.title: Common Cat Hazards
sources.readStatus: Plants, medication, poisoning signs, and action sections read
excerpts: Human medications and flea treatments for dogs can be acutely toxic for cats.
Call your veterinarian immediately.
DO NOT induce vomiting unless you are specifically directed to do so.
sources.limits: The page is US-facing. Do not copy US poison telephone numbers into the Australian app. It does not name permethrin; use the RSPCA source for that specific chemical. Not every plant with 'lily' in its common name causes the same renal toxicity.
recommendedCorrections: Keep immediate veterinary contact and the warning not to induce vomiting. Replace vague clinic-source labels with the exact source URL.

sources.title: Are lilies toxic to cats?
sources.readStatus: Full article body and references read
excerpts: Lily toxicity in cats is an emergency.
All parts of the lily plant are toxic, including petals, stems, leaves, and pollen
even the water in a vase of cut lilies is thought to be toxic
sources.limits: Keep scientific names Lilium and Hemerocallis. The page's common-name list includes names that can be botanically ambiguous; do not turn that list into a claim that all plants called lilies cause identical kidney injury.
recommendedCorrections: Keep immediate care for suspected exposure, including pollen grooming and vase water. Tell owners not to wait for symptoms.
For an unidentified 'lily', contact a vet and provide a plant photograph or label. Use the current Knowledgebase URL.

sources.title: What are common household dangers for pets?
sources.readStatus: Permethrin and medication sections read
excerpts: If you suspect your cat has been exposed to permethrin, contact your veterinarian immediately.
It is particularly toxic to cats, even in tiny amounts
Ibuprofen, another common human pain medication, can be severely toxic to dogs and cats
sources.supports: The second excerpt refers to paracetamol. The permethrin section also reports toxicity after close contact with treated dogs.
sources.limits: Symptoms are not required before seeking care. Product dose, species label, minimum age, current weight, and contact precautions matter.
recommendedCorrections: Change the permethrin card to act on suspected exposure, not only tremors, twitching, drooling, or seizures.
Replace the 'not yet verified against RSPCA/AVA' source with this read RSPCA page.

sources.title: Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
sources.readStatus: Breed predisposition, clinical signs, diagnosis, and genetic-test cautions read
excerpts: more prevalent in certain breeds (including Maine Coon, Ragdoll, British Shorthair, American Shorthair, Sphynx, Bengal, Chartreux, Norwegian Forest, Siberian, and Persian cats)
not all cats that have these mutations will develop the condition
causing acute hind limb pain or, in extreme cases, hind limb paralysis
sources.limits: Breed predisposition is not a diagnosis. Echocardiography establishes HCM; gene screening is not a full substitute. The page supports thromboembolism as a cause of acute hind-limb signs, not the only cause.
recommendedCorrections: Keep HCM risk notes for Persian, Maine Coon, Ragdoll, Bengal, and British Shorthair. Add Sphynx, which currently has an empty risk list.
Keep sudden painful hind-limb weakness as an emergency. Replace the unverified case-report citation with Cornell.
Do not claim that a negative breed-specific genetic test rules out HCM.

sources.title: Myosin-binding protein C DNA variants in domestic cats (A31P, A74T, R820W) and their association with Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
sources.publisher: Journal of Veterinary Internal Medicine; Longeri et al.
sources.readStatus: Abstract, introduction, genotype results, and diagnostic limitations read
excerpts: The MYBPC3 A31P and R820W were restricted to MCO and RD respectively.
Both purebred and random bred cats had HCM
Penetrance is incomplete for heterozygotes at A31P locus, at least at a young age.
sources.limits: MCO means Maine Coon; RD means Ragdoll. This is a 2013 study, not a current catalogue of all feline HCM genes or currently available tests. UC Davis current test pages were discoverable in search but returned 403 to direct fetch.
recommendedCorrections: Say 'A breed-associated variant can be tested; ask your vet about genetic testing and heart screening.' Avoid 'the gene' as if all disease in the breed has one cause.
For Bengal, keep the increased-risk statement. Remove the absolute current claim that the responsible gene has not been identified unless checked against an up-to-date genetic reference.

sources.title: Polycystic Kidney Disease
sources.readStatus: Page body read
excerpts: Occurring most frequently in Persian cats, polycystic kidney disease is an inherited disorder
primarily in Persians and occasionally in a few other feline breeds, such as Himalayans and British Shorthairs
sources.limits: Do not convert breed association into an individual diagnosis or quote outdated prevalence. The source discusses genetic testing and ultrasound; severity cannot be inferred from a gene result alone.
recommendedCorrections: Keep the Persian and British Shorthair PKD notes and attach this exact URL.

sources.title: Mapping the genetic basis of diabetes mellitus in the Australian Burmese cat (Felis catus)
sources.publisher: Scientific Reports; Samaha et al., University of Sydney and collaborators
sources.readStatus: Abstract and introduction read; linked correction also read
excerpts: In Australia and Europe, diabetes mellitus is almost four times more common among Burmese cats than in other breeds.
the same heightened risk has not been observed in the North American Burmese population
sources.limits: Risk differs by breeding population. The 2021 correction changes LOX2 to LOXL2; it does not change the breed-risk claim.
recommendedCorrections: Keep a higher diabetes-risk note for Burmese in the Australian app. Add the population qualifier and exact source.

sources.title: Renal Amyloidosis
sources.readStatus: Page body read
excerpts: renal amyloidosis is a rare condition
the condition also occurs with disproportionate frequency in Oriental breeds
sources.supports: The page identifies Abyssinian cats as especially associated with renal amyloidosis.
sources.limits: The source supports Abyssinian and Oriental risk; it does not establish identical risk for every cat within the app's combined Siamese / Oriental option.
recommendedCorrections: Consider a qualified renal amyloidosis note for Abyssinian and Oriental cats.
Do not display an empty risk list as 'no inherited risks'. Use 'No breed-specific notes included' and state that the list is not complete.

sources.title: How can I protect my dog or cat from tick paralysis?
sources.readStatus: Prevention, distribution, clinical signs, and emergency action sections read
excerpts: Ticks can also be found inland in suitable habitats.
at least once a day even if tick control products have been applied
Do not offer food or water or give anything orally

supports.distribution: Eastern seaboard from North Queensland to Victoria; also suitable inland habitat
supports.action: Immediate veterinary attention for suspected paralysis or a tick/crater

sources.limits: The oral-intake warning applies to pets affected by tick paralysis. Northern exposure can be year-round; southern season varies. This page does not verify the app's exact 24–48-hour post-removal progression claim. It does not prove the ACT is tick-free.
recommendedCorrections: Do not suppress tick advice solely because region is ACT or other. Include local habitat and travel to tick areas in the vet discussion.
Keep cat-labelled prevention, daily searches, and immediate care. Add the no-food/water warning for suspected paralysis.
Remove the precise post-removal time claim unless supported by a separately read veterinary source.

sources.title: How do I stop my companion animal from getting fleas?
sources.readStatus: Prevention and treatment section read
excerpts: Use a flea preventative product throughout the year.
Your veterinarian can give you advice about the most suitable product for your pet and how often this should be applied.
Flea preventative products designed for dogs can be fatal if given to cats.
sources.limits: RSPCA does not set one monthly interval for every product. All pets and the environment may need treatment during an infestation.
recommendedCorrections: Keep year-round prevention and cat-safe products. Lead with the product-label interval, not a universal monthly interval.

sources.title: Parasite Control in Kittens and Cats
sources.readStatus: Intestinal worms, fleas, and combination products sections read
excerpts: every two weeks until 12 weeks of age, then monthly until six months of age, and thereafter every three months
sources.limits: One Australian clinic's general schedule, not a national guideline or universal prescription. The article has no publication date. Some broad product claims may be stale. Worm species and product coverage differ.
recommendedCorrections: Use a clearly labelled example: two-weekly to 12 weeks, then monthly to six months; vet-set adult intervals.
Do not retain vague 'varies by source' as the only citation. Link an actual read source and preserve the vet/product qualification.
Do not assume a combination product covers tapeworm, heartworm, and every intestinal worm.

sources.title: Does my cat need heartworm prevention?
sources.publisher: Andrew Spanner BVSc(Hons) MVetStud, Walkerville Vet, Adelaide
sources.readStatus: Main article and dated vet replies read
excerpts: no approved treatment once a cat acquires heartworm
sources.limits: The article recommends prevention, while an October 2020 reply says local risk had become low enough to omit it for cats. This is local, dated clinical opinion, not current ACT prevalence. No read AVA source established the app's attributed national claim.
recommendedCorrections: Keep heartworm prevention as a discussion with the local vet. Do not claim an AVA schedule or derive risk solely from the three region choices.
Use cat-registered products. Do not import dog yearly-injection advice into cat care.

sources.title: Cats
sources.readStatus: Registration, microchipping, desexing, containment, suburb list, and multiple-cat sections read
excerpts: Each year you must renew your registration, free of charge.
All cats in the ACT must be microchipped.
Containment means keeping your cat on your premises 24 hours a day.
A multiple cat licence is required if a person wishes to keep 4 or more cats on a residential property.

supports.registration: Cats over 8 weeks; cat and keeper each in ACT for at least 28 days
supports.initialRegistration: One-time fee stated on the current page
desexingExceptions: Keeper holds a sexually entire permit

sources.limits: The current page says cats born 'after 1 July 2022'; the app says 'on or after'. The exact statutory birthday boundary was not resolved in this pass. The page is official guidance, not a full legal review. Fees and suburb boundaries can change.
recommendedCorrections: Use the current canonical URL and access date. Keep the annual renewal wording; do not imply initial registration is free.
Check the legislation before resolving the exact 1 July birth-date boundary.
Link the live containment map rather than depending only on a suburb count.
Consider the four-or-more-cats licence rule. Use an exact source record rather than a broad 'verified' flag.

sources.title: The Complete Feeding Guide From Kittens to Seniors
sources.author: Jackie Brown
sources.readStatus: Byline, nutritional adequacy, newborn, weaning, kitten, adult, and senior sections read
excerpts: Kittens require a kitten milk replacement formula
Do not feed a kitten cow’s milk
there’s no single amount of food that every cat should eat each day
sources.limits: Vet-reviewed secondary owner guide, not the primary formula authority. Age-based amounts are estimates; chart and narrative are not entirely consistent. Do not use the general calculator for nursing or bottle-fed kittens.
recommendedCorrections: Add as further reading with title, author, reviewer, date, and direct link. Keep AAHA as the calculator source.
For pre-weaning kittens, show a vet/kitten-care referral rather than a dry/wet solid-food plan.

sources.title: How Much to Feed a Cat
sources.author: Dr. Pete Wedderburn, DVM
sources.readStatus: Byline, formula, factor table, feeding schedule, and monitoring sections read
excerpts: RER=70 x (body weight in kg/lbs) to the power of 0.75
Neutered adult cat | 1.6 x RER
Cat aiming to lose weight | 1.0 x RER for ideal weight
sources.limits: The displayed kg/lbs wording is incorrect for this coefficient: kilograms are required. Its adult and weight-loss factors differ from AAHA 2021 feline Box 1. Do not cite this page as agreement with the app's AAHA factors.
recommendedCorrections: Use only as a qualified secondary reading link, or prefer the vet-reviewed life-stage guide. Do not replace AAHA factors with this table.

sources.title: 25 Tips for First-Time Cat Owners
sources.author: Dr. Lizzie Youens BSc (Hons) BVSc MRCVS
sources.readStatus: Byline, food, diet change, hydration, health, litter, bonding, and enrichment content read
excerpts: transition slowly over the course of a week
The exact ingredients, flavors, and type of food are less important than the choice of a nutritionally complete diet suitable for your cat’s age.
sources.limits: Veterinarian-written secondary guide. 'Fact checked' is not the same as an independent clinical review. Its broad dry-food dental-benefit statement should not be imported as proof that ordinary kibble cleans teeth.
recommendedCorrections: Add as further reading for new owners. Use AAFP/ISFM for environmental claims and primary clinical sources for emergency advice.

priorityCorrections.change: Remove the few-minute waiting threshold. Abnormal breathing needs immediate veterinary contact.
Do not tell owners to wait beyond 24 hours. Seek prompt advice, sooner for kittens or sick cats. Remove the exact one-to-two-day lipidosis claim.
Act on suspected exposure even before symptoms.
Distinguish long-lived FPV protection from risk-dependent FHV/FCV boosters. Do not give one three-year rule for all cats.
Exclude pre-weaning kittens and require vet guidance for illness, pregnancy, lactation, underweight cats, and weight loss.
The 1% rate and linear weeks-to-target are illustrative assumptions, not validated outcome predictions.
Count treats and extras within total daily kcal and keep them at or below 10%.
Use local risk, travel, cat-labelled products, and exact read sources. ACT is not proved tick-free.
Add source links and a non-exhaustive label. Sphynx HCM and Abyssinian amyloidosis are supported omissions.

unresolvedOrNotValidated: AAHA 2014 official weight-management PDF was discoverable but direct download returned 403. The weekly range was read in AAHA 2026 and a peer-reviewed review that cites AAHA 2014.
UC Davis current HCM and PKD test pages returned 403. Do not mark those pages directly read. Current test availability needs an accessible laboratory page or vet confirmation.
No current primary ACT parasite-prevalence dataset or exact Australian AVA heartworm schedule was read.
TroCCAP feline endoparasite PDF returned 406; it was not used as read evidence.
The exact 1 July 2022 statutory containment birthday boundary needs checking against current ACT legislation.

Exact 10–15-minute play sessions, fixed tooth-brushing training days, nail-trim frequency, paper-ink restrictions, shopping costs, hairless-cat skin wipes, and every breed-specific disease were not validated in this pass.
The dailyRoutine Weekly label conflicts with its monthly weigh-in text. Select frequency by purpose: routine monitoring versus a vet-supervised weight-loss plan.
This source pass did not run code, assess all input-validation paths, inspect the rendered app, verify links through the UI, or obtain veterinary sign-off.
